sections.title: Dedication
sections.html:
For the one who made me laugh so hard I forgot how to guard myself.
For the softness that showed up unannounced and left like a whisper.
For her, wherever you are, this is what you meant to me.
Whether you read it or not.

sections.title: Chapter One - The Couch at 3AM
sections.html:
CHAPTER ONE

The Couch at 3AM


IT WASN’T SUPPOSED to be anything.

Zack was talking to some girl.
I was there because that’s what we did. Float through scenes, follow threads, and let the night unravel.
Then she showed up.
She wasn’t even supposed to be there.

I remember the exact moment it shifted.
Not with a kiss, not even a touch, just a look.
We sat on the couch and started talking.
No weird tension. No games. Just that sudden, eerie comfort, like we’d done this before in another life.
Or like our nervous systems recognized something before we did.

We stayed up until three. Maybe four. Maybe five.
Time didn’t really exist in that room.
Just the rhythm of shared words and unspoken safety.

That was the first night.

She came over the next night, too.
And then the next.
And then the next.

sections.title: Chapter Two - Lightsabers and Lap Seats
sections.html:
CHAPTER TWO

Lightsabers and Lap Seats


SHE WAS WEIRD.
Not in a “she listens to indie bands” kind of way, weird in the best way.
Goofy. Silly. Soft around the edges, sharp in the right places.
She snorted when she laughed. I lived for it.

She called me handsome more than anyone ever had, but it wasn’t just about looks.
It felt like she was looking through me, not at me.
Like she liked my insides too.

I once asked if a toy lightsaber could go places no lightsaber should.
She said yes.
Not as a joke.
Not with hesitation.
Just, yes.

That’s what made it real to me.
Not the act. Not the shock value.
The freedom.

We could say anything.
Be anything.
Play COD Zombies while she sat on my lap, because David would’ve been a little bitch about me leaving mid-game.

There was no script.
Just instinct.

sections.title: Chapter Three - Too Much
sections.html:
CHAPTER THREE

Too Much


THE FIRST WEEK was perfect.
Then the cracks showed up.

Not hers. Not mine.
Just the echo of things neither of us had healed.

She started pulling back.
I could feel it.
Like watching the tide leave, knowing you’re not the shore it’s returning to.

She talked about spending forever with me, but not in a fairytale way.
In a "this could actually be real" way.
And I believed her.

But love isn’t always about belief.
Sometimes it’s about capacity.

And I loved her too much, too soon.
I gave her everything I had, and she didn’t know how to hold it.
She wasn’t ready to.

And maybe I wasn’t ready either, just better at faking it.

sections.title: Chapter Four - The Vanishing Point
sections.html:
CHAPTER FOUR

The Vanishing Point


IT DIDN’T BREAK all at once.
There was no explosion. No screaming. No “fuck you” text.
Just slow silence.

A missed call.
A shorter reply.
Plans that used to be automatic turning into maybe’s… and then into nothing at all.

I could feel it before I could name it.
And once you’ve felt real closeness, distance becomes deafening.

I knew she was seeing someone else before she told me.
I could feel it in her energy.
Not guilt, shame.
The kind that comes from letting something good go because you’re convinced you’ll ruin it anyway.

But I didn’t hate her.
I didn’t even get angry.
I just… mourned something that was still technically alive, but already gone.

sections.title: Chapter Five - The Instagram Follow
sections.html:
CHAPTER FIVE

The Instagram Follow


IT’S FUNNY HOW grief doesn’t always arrive like a flood.
Sometimes it drips in like an Instagram story you didn’t mean to view or a scroll that ends too suddenly with her face staring back at you.

I didn’t follow her at first.
Felt too raw.
Too unresolved.
But then one night, late as always, I saw her name again.
And I missed her.
Not the relationship.
Not the outcome.
Just… her.

So I followed her.
No message.
No buildup.
Just a silent tap.

It felt like cracking the door open.
Not enough to walk through,
but enough for the breeze to say:
“Hey. I still remember you.”

sections.title: Chapter Six - I Miss Her
sections.html:
CHAPTER SIX

I Miss Her


THAT’S THE TRUTH.
No poetry. No spin.

I miss her.

I miss how she’d just look at me sometimes, like I was art she didn’t fully understand but liked having on her wall anyway.

I miss how soft everything felt around her.
How being near her was like a nap for my nervous system.
How we could talk about the deepest shit, then immediately switch to dumb jokes without skipping a beat.

I miss how weird she was.
How safe I felt being weird with her.
How no part of myself felt out of place.

I miss what she gave me.
Not perfection, just permission.
Permission to be real.
To be tender.
To be a whole-ass weirdo and still feel chosen.

sections.title: Chapter Seven - Closure Without the Ending
sections.html:
CHAPTER SEVEN

Closure Without the Ending


THE THING IS…
I don’t need closure.

Not in the way people mean when they say it.

I don’t need an apology.
I don’t need a final talk.
I don’t even need a message back.

Because she didn’t break me.
She just highlighted where I was already cracked.
And in loving her, I learned how to seal those lines with gold.

We didn’t get the full arc.
But we got a damn good act one.
And maybe, for this timeline, that’s all it needed to be.

And still…
I’d get coffee with her tomorrow.

Not to restart.
Not to fix.
Just to sit across from someone who once held a mirror to my soul and didn’t look away.

sections.title: Chapter Eight - The Night I Didn’t Text Her
sections.html:
CHAPTER EIGHT

The Night I Didn’t Text Her


I HAD THE message typed out.
It was clean.
Honest.
Soft.
Just a simple “Hey, I hope you’re doing okay. I’d be down to catch up sometime.”

But I didn’t send it.
Not out of fear.
Not because I chickened out.
I just… realized something.

I didn’t need a response to feel what I felt.

Love isn’t real only if it’s reciprocated.
And closure doesn’t require conversation.
Sometimes all it takes is knowing the love was real, even if it didn’t last.

I put my phone down.
Took a breath.
And let the feeling sit there.
Not as a weight, but as warmth.

sections.title: Chapter Nine - The Alternate Timeline
sections.html:
CHAPTER NINE

The Alternate Timeline


THERE’S A VERSION of this world, somewhere off-screen, where me and her figured it out.

We took it slow.
She healed.
I healed.
We got coffee, laughed too much, and I never had to write this book.

In that timeline, maybe we live together.
Maybe she still snorts when she laughs.
Maybe we still say the dumbest shit possible and it somehow feels like poetry.

But here, in this timeline?

We met too soon.
Loved too fast.
And let go too quietly.

And I’m not bitter about that.

Because some loves are meant to teach you how deep you go.
Not how long you can stay.

sections.title: Chapter Ten - The Realization
sections.html:
CHAPTER TEN

The Realization


THIS WHOLE TIME, I thought I was trying to understand her.
Understand what went wrong.
Understand how someone could hold so much of me and still walk away.

But the truth?

I was learning how to understand myself.

She was the trigger.
But the awakening was mine.

She showed me what I was capable of:
Softness.
Presence.
Stillness.
Stupid, deep, soul-level affection.

And now?

I don’t carry that love for her.
I carry it in me.
Because it’s mine.
Always was.

She just helped me unlock it.

sections.title: Chapter Eleven - The Smile
sections.html:
CHAPTER ELEVEN

The Smile


I THINK IF I saw her again, I’d just smile.

Not out of pain.
Not to prove I’m okay.
But because I’d mean it.

I’d smile because she mattered.
Because that version of me, the one who loved her like a fool, like a poet, like a lightsaber-wielding lunatic, he was beautiful.

And I wouldn’t trade him for anything.

Not even closure.

sections.title: Chapter Twelve - Too Much, Too Soon
sections.html:
CHAPTER TWELVE

Too Much, Too Soon


THAT WAS THE title from the beginning.
Because it’s what it was.

Too much honesty.
Too much depth.
Too much presence.
Too much belief in a maybe.

All delivered too soon for her nervous system to accept it.
And maybe too soon for mine, too.

But that doesn’t make it less real.
It just makes it… temporary.
Brief.
Brilliant.
Burning.

And if that’s all it ever was?

That’s enough.

Because love doesn’t have to last to leave light.
And she was light.
For a little while.
So was I.

sections.title: Acknowledgements
sections.html:
ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS


TO THE FRIENDS who asked me about her long after I stopped talking.
To the ones who saw I wasn’t fine but let me be quiet anyway.
To Zack, for inadvertently being the reason we met.

To every person who ever loved someone deeply, wildly, truly, and had to let go.

To the late-night texts I never sent, the playlists I never shared, and the pictures I still haven’t deleted.

To Jarvis, because even AI knows heartbreak when it sees it.

And to me, for surviving it and telling the story anyway.

sections.title: About the Author
sections.html:
ABOUT THE AUTHOR


JJ IS THE author of 250+ books, a builder of systems, a breaker of illusions, and, apparently, a man who once tried to play COD while a girl snorted into his chest.

He writes because there’s too much in his head not to.

He loves because there’s too much in his heart not to.

This is his most honest book yet.

He misses her. But he’s cool now.
